description: A business operating accommodation management and associated letting or caretaking rights. Excludes general real estate agencies. The activity is the contracted accommodation-management, letting or caretaking operation. Ownership of an apartment or holiday unit alone is insufficient; general third-party real estate management has its own category.

Operation of a caravan, camping or holiday park, including associated cabins and site services. Includes managed sites for touring caravans, campers and associated holiday cabins. A land holding without an operating park is different; permanent retirement accommodation belongs in the relevant living or care category.

category_name: Guest Houses and Bed and Breakfast
description: Visitor accommodation in a guest house or bed-and-breakfast establishment. Excludes permanent residential care. Includes small hosted guest accommodation and comparable owner-operated lodging establishments. Classification follows the accommodation operation, rather than ownership of a residential property or a property-management investment alone.

Budget visitor accommodation primarily in hostels or backpacker lodgings, commonly with shared facilities. Covers operating the accommodation business and its guest services, rather than selling the building alone. A separately operated cafe, tour service or other substantial activity may justify an additional category.

Operation of a hotel primarily providing short-stay accommodation. A venue primarily operating as a pub or bar uses Pubs, Bars and Nightclubs. Includes accommodation-led hotels with associated guest facilities. Where the business is primarily a pub or nightlife venue, use that activity even if some rooms are available; a property-only sale is outside this scope.

Operation of a motel primarily providing short-stay accommodation for travellers. Includes traveller accommodation typically sold by room for short stays. Associated food services can be additional activities when substantial; an investment in the premises alone does not identify a motel operating business.

Operation of visitor accommodation with substantial integrated leisure or holiday facilities. Examples include holiday accommodation with integrated recreation, dining and guest amenities. The resort operation is primary; independent tour, retail or hospitality businesses should be classified by their own activities.

Operation of an admission-based theme or amusement park with permanent attractions. Includes operating a destination with permanent themed rides or attractions. Prefer the more specific children's play category for an indoor play centre; event performers and equipment hire are different operations.

Operation of guided visitor tours, excursions or sightseeing experiences. Excludes an agency primarily reselling other operators' travel. Includes guided sightseeing and activity-based excursions sold as an organised visitor experience. Transport can be integral to the tour; add a transport category only for a separate passenger-carriage activity.

Travel agency, booking and travel arrangement services. Excludes operators primarily conducting their own tours or passenger transport. Includes businesses arranging bookings and travel products supplied by other operators. Conducting the operator's own tour or carrying passengers is a different activity, even when sold through the same booking channel.

Aircraft maintenance, repair and associated technical support services. Excludes air transport, recreational flight experiences and aircraft dealers. Includes technical aircraft maintenance, repair and support businesses. Identify whether customers purchase equipment, maintenance or carriage; ownership of aircraft and an aviation customer base alone do not identify the operation.

Sale and supply of aircraft and aviation equipment. Excludes aircraft maintenance, passenger/freight carriage and recreational flight experiences. Includes aircraft dealerships, aviation equipment sales and related technical product supply. Determine whether the business sells equipment, maintains aircraft or carries passengers; the word aviation alone cannot distinguish these roles.

Installation, diagnosis and repair of electrical and electronic systems in motor vehicles. Excludes general building electrical work. Examples include vehicle wiring, starting/charging systems and electronic diagnostics. Repair of vehicle systems belongs here; manufacture of components, retail-only parts sales and building electrical contracting remain separate activities.

Sale, servicing or repair of bicycles and motorcycles. Excludes a business primarily hiring recreational equipment. Includes specialist bicycle and motorcycle dealers and service workshops. Electric variants follow the same activity; vehicle technology alone does not create another category, and unrelated car dealerships or freight operators are excluded.

Sale and supply of boats, marine engines and related equipment. Prefer Marine Maintenance for maintenance and repair; excludes water transport and recreational marine experiences. Examples include boat dealerships and marine engine/accessory supply. A repair yard or boat maintenance contractor belongs under Marine Maintenance; charter experiences and passenger or freight carriage have separate scopes.

Sale of new or used passenger motor vehicles through a dealership. Excludes vehicle hire and truck-only dealers. Includes dealerships primarily earning from passenger-car sales. A substantial repair workshop or finance activity can be identified separately; selling business vehicles incidentally is insufficient to classify another business as a dealership.

Hire of passenger motor vehicles to customers. Excludes chauffeured transport and freight operations. Includes fleets hired to customers for self-drive use. A driver-supplied passenger service belongs under Taxi and Chauffeur Services; trading vehicles or renting accommodation is a different activity.

Operation of a vehicle washing business, including automated or self-service facilities. Prefer Detailing for specialist finishing and restoration. Includes staffed, automated and self-service vehicle wash operations. Specialist finishing and protection work can use Detailing; mobile delivery changes neither activity nor the distinction between washing and body repair.

Specialist vehicle cleaning, polishing, surface protection and cosmetic detailing. Excludes panel repairs and routine mechanical repairs. Examples include intensive interior treatment, polishing and protective surface applications. Choose Vehicle Body Repairs for collision work; routine washing alone does not establish a specialist detailing business.

Instruction in driving road vehicles, including learner and commercial driver training. Includes businesses selling road-driver instruction and associated practical lessons. General vocational training can be additional only when separately substantial; vehicle ownership or hire alone does not establish an instruction business.

Boat and marine equipment maintenance, repair and technical services. Excludes boat dealers, sea transport and marine leisure experiences. Includes technical servicing, repair and maintenance of boats, engines and marine equipment. Sales, charters, leisure experiences and transport are different activities, even when the business owns vessels or waterfront premises.

Retail sale of vehicle fuel through a service station, with or without an associated convenience shop. Includes operating a fuel-retail forecourt, with associated goods sales or amenities. A substantial convenience store may be another activity; wholesale fuel supply, extraction and electricity-generation businesses are different operations.

Sale of commercial trucks and truck equipment. Excludes truck freight operators and general mechanical workshops. Includes dealers supplying commercial trucks and related equipment. Distinguish selling a truck from carrying a customer's freight or repairing a fleet; those businesses belong in transport or workshop categories.

Repair and refinishing of vehicle bodies after damage, including collision and panel work. Includes collision body repair, panel work and vehicle refinishing. Cosmetic detailing without repair uses Detailing; general mechanical servicing and selling replacement parts are different activities even when performed at the same premises.

Dismantling vehicles and recovering used vehicle parts for resale or recycling. Includes recovering saleable vehicle components and materials from dismantled vehicles. General waste recovery is separate when broader materials processing is primary; an ordinary used-car dealership is not a dismantling operation.

Mechanical servicing and repair of road vehicles, including tyre fitting and wheel servicing. Excludes workshops primarily doing auto electrical or collision body repairs; a distinct parts sales activity can also use Vehicle Parts and Accessories. Includes servicing workshops, tyre fitting and wheel work where technical vehicle maintenance is primary. Vehicle sales, parts retail, auto electrical work and collision repairs can be separate categories when distinct operations genuinely exist.

Sale or distribution of motor vehicle parts and accessories, including tyres and wheels. Excludes vehicle manufacture and general repair workshops. A distinct fitting/servicing activity can also use Vehicle Mechanical Repairs. Includes specialist tyre, wheel, aftermarket and replacement-parts businesses. The product-sales role differs from fitting or mechanical servicing; selecting both requires actual sales and service activities, rather than incidental consumables used in repairs.

Provision of beauty treatments through a salon, excluding businesses primarily offering hair, nails, massage or spa services. Examples include facial, skin-care and general beauty-treatment businesses. A hair, nail, massage or spa operation should use its named category when primary; selling beauty products alone is retail or wholesale supply.

Hairdressing, barbering and associated hair salon services. Excludes businesses primarily selling hair products. Includes hairdressing salons and barber businesses, whether appointment-based or walk-in. A separate beauty-treatment or product-trading activity can justify another category; the sale of consumables incidental to a service is insufficient by itself.

Operation of a health or beauty spa providing a combination of relaxation and personal treatments. Excludes hospital and medical care. Includes spas primarily selling a coordinated relaxation or personal-treatment experience. Accommodation-led resorts, medical clinics and standalone massage or beauty salons should use their more informative primary activity.

Provision of massage services. Excludes physiotherapy practices and businesses primarily operating a broader spa. Includes businesses primarily selling massage sessions and related non-equipment services. Physiotherapy remains a distinct clinical practice; an incidental massage offering within a broader spa does not require duplicate classification.

Provision of manicure, pedicure and nail salon services. Includes businesses primarily providing nail-care appointments and related salon work. Other independently substantial beauty or retail activities can be combined; selling nail products to consumers or salons is a separate trading role.

Provision of complementary or natural therapy services. The category makes no claim about treatment efficacy or professional recognition. Includes practices primarily offering complementary or natural-therapy services, rather than selling products. Record the actual service being operated.

Operation of childcare, early learning or out-of-school-hours care services. Excludes a business primarily selling children's products. Includes operating early-learning, childcare and out-of-school care businesses. Children's play venues, tuition, retail products and clinical support have their own scopes; serving children is not sufficient to select childcare.

Provision of education, tutoring or learning services not better described by Child Care or vocational/professional Training. Delivery online does not create a separate industry. Examples include tutoring, subject tuition and general learning providers. Use Vocational and Professional Training for employment-related skills programmes; online delivery and the age of learners do not themselves establish another industry.

Provision of vocational, professional or skills training. Excludes recruitment and general school-subject tutoring; online delivery does not change the activity. Examples include trade, workplace and professional-skills course providers. Delivery can be in person or online; course format does not establish accreditation, and staffing placement remains Recruitment and Staffing.

Production and sale of bakery goods through a bakery business. Excludes general food factories not primarily operating as a bakery. Includes baking operations with their own bakery retail outlet. An independently substantial cafe can be combined; a general food factory or shop merely reselling packaged bakery products should use the appropriate production or retail activity.

Preparation and retail sale of meat through a butcher shop. Excludes livestock farming and broad food manufacturing. Includes meat preparation and retail through butcher shops. Livestock production, commercial food processing and trade wholesale remain separate; a deli offering alone does not require every food-retail category.

Operation of a cafe or coffee shop primarily serving beverages and light meals. Excludes packaged coffee supply without a hospitality outlet. Examples include coffee shops and light-meal cafes. Combine with Bakery or a children's play operation when those are distinct businesses; coffee sold incidentally by an unrelated retailer does not establish a cafe.

Preparation and supply of food for events or customers away from a regular dine-in venue. Excludes venues primarily hired for functions. Includes preparing and supplying food for private, corporate and other events, often at customer or hired locations. Venue operation and event planning can be separate activities; carrying prepared food alone is transport rather than catering.

Operation of a small general grocery and convenience shop. Prefer Service Station where vehicle fuel is the main activity. Includes neighbourhood convenience outlets with a mixed everyday grocery range. Choose Service Station where fuel retail is primary and Supermarket for a broad supermarket operation; opening hours alone do not determine classification.

Retail sale of delicatessen foods, prepared meats, cheeses and related products, with or without food preparation. Includes deli shops primarily supplying specialist prepared foods, cured products and related items. Cafe service, meat butchery or wholesale should be additional categories only where each is a distinct substantial activity.

Retail sale of fresh fruit and vegetables. Excludes growing produce and general supermarkets. Includes greengrocers and similar outlets primarily selling fresh produce to consumers. Growing produce and supplying trade customers belong in farming or wholesale; general grocery stores are better described by their broader retail format.

Operation of a juice or smoothie bar primarily preparing beverages for immediate consumption. Includes outlets primarily preparing juices, smoothies and comparable fresh drinks for immediate consumption. Bottled beverage manufacturing or distribution is different; a broader cafe should use the cafe category when that describes the main operation.

Retail sale of packaged alcoholic beverages through a liquor business. Excludes venues primarily serving drinks for consumption on site. Includes bottle shops and other outlets selling packaged alcoholic drinks to consumers. On-premises consumption-led venues use the pub/bar or restaurant category; wholesale distribution is a separate trading role.

Operation of a restaurant primarily preparing and serving meals for consumption on the premises. Includes dining establishments whose main operation is prepared meals served on site. A substantial takeaway operation may also be relevant; cuisine names and a delivery platform alone do not require separate categories.

Specialist food or beverage retail not better described by a named shop category. Excludes hospitality and wholesale supply. Use for specialist consumer food shops not captured by the named bakery, butcher, deli, produce, liquor or grocery categories. Explain the main product range; a broad category should not replace a known more informative shop type.

Operation of a supermarket offering a broad range of groceries and household goods. Includes supermarkets supplying a broad grocery and household range. A small convenience outlet or specialist food shop has a different format; food manufacture and trade wholesale are separate business activities.

Preparation and sale of takeaway or quick-service food, including mobile food outlets. Excludes a business primarily providing event catering. Examples include primarily takeaway pizza, burger and fish-and-chip outlets, including food vans. Choose Restaurant where dine-in meal service is primary; mobility, cuisine and online ordering do not establish another industry by themselves.

Wholesale and trade supply of beauty, cosmetic and salon products. Consumer shops use Health and Beauty Retail; manufacturers use the relevant manufacturing category. Includes trade businesses buying and supplying beauty or salon products to business customers. Consumer shops, treatment providers and manufacturers have separate roles; identify the main customer and supply activity before classifying the operation.

Customs brokerage, clearance and related trade documentation services. Excludes businesses primarily carrying freight or trading goods. The core service is customs clearance, brokerage and trade documentation for clients. Freight forwarding or carriage can be additional activities when genuinely operated; importing the business's own stock alone does not make it a customs broker.

Buying and reselling food or beverage stock to trade customers. Excludes freight-only delivery and general wholesale of non-food goods. Includes buying and reselling food or drink stock to business customers, often with associated distribution. Freight-only carriage, food manufacture and consumer retail are different roles; identify stock trading rather than simply the movement of goods.

Buying and reselling goods to trade customers where a more specific product wholesale category does not apply. Excludes retail-only and freight-only businesses. Use for trade stock-reselling businesses without a more informative product wholesale category. Identify whether customers are businesses and whether the operator trades the goods; retail-only shops and carriage-only contractors are not wholesale activities.

Trade businesses primarily sourcing or supplying goods across borders. Prefer a product wholesale category where more informative; excludes freight and customs services. Includes stock-trading businesses whose main role is import, export or both. Identify the direction of trade and product range; brokerage, carrying freight and selling the operator's own locally produced output are different roles.

Manufacture of electrical equipment or components. Use Electrical in Construction and Trades for installation and maintenance contracting. Includes businesses making electrical equipment or components, rather than installing them at customer sites. A dealer, technical service contractor and manufacturer can serve the same industry while operating different business activities.

Manufacture or processing of food and beverages. Excludes hospitality outlets preparing meals primarily for their own customers. Includes commercial production and processing of food or drink for supply beyond the operator's own hospitality outlet. Trade wholesale, farming and consumer food retail are distinct stages and can be combined only for actual additional activities.

Manufacture or processing of furniture, timber products and associated joinery. Excludes furniture-only retail. Includes production of furniture, timber goods and associated joinery. Furniture shops and building installation services remain separate; a combined maker/retailer can identify both actual activities without treating every supplier as a manufacturer.

Manufacturing and production engineering businesses not better described by a specific product category. Excludes consultancy without production activity. Use for genuine manufacturing or production engineering without a suitable named product category. Identify the output being made; design-only consultancy, recovery of waste without production and ordinary repair work are different operations.

Manufacture or processing of glass and ceramic products. Excludes general retail of finished household goods. Examples include businesses producing or processing glassware, ceramic goods and relevant components. A shop selling finished household goods or a contractor installing glazing should be classified by the actual trading or service activity.

Manufacture or fabrication of machinery and metal products. Excludes equipment dealers and machinery repair-only businesses. Includes machinery production and metal-product fabrication. Selling equipment, maintaining machines or supplying welding services alone are different activities; choose the more informative production category where the product is known.

Mining services, extraction support and earthmoving operations. Use Civil for businesses primarily delivering civil infrastructure works. Includes specialist earthmoving, extraction-support and mining-contract operations. Prefer Civil for integrated civil infrastructure delivery; technical advice or sale of earthmoving equipment alone is not the same activity.

Manufacture of paper, board, containers and packaging products. Excludes customer print/signage services and waste recovery as the main activity. Includes factories producing paper, board, packaging and containers for onward supply. A customer print shop or a waste-paper recovery business operates at another stage and should not be assigned this manufacturing category solely from its material.

Manufacture or processing of plastic products and components. Excludes plastic waste recovery as the main activity. Includes production and processing of finished plastic goods or components. A distributor of finished products or a recycler recovering materials without manufacturing new goods should use its actual trading or recovery activity.

Manufacture of clothing, footwear or associated textile products. Excludes consumer fashion retail. Includes factories and production businesses making garments, footwear and textile products. Retail, trade wholesale and alteration or repair services are different roles; a fabric or fashion product label alone does not establish manufacturing.

Adult entertainment venues or services. Excludes ordinary leisure venues and general retail. Includes businesses primarily providing adult entertainment services or operating associated venues. Ordinary nightlife, general entertainment and retail products have different scopes; classify the operated activity rather than a broad marketing description.

Operation of amusement, arcade or entertainment attractions. Prefer Children's Play and Activity Centres for a play-centre business and Theme Park for permanent themed attractions. Includes arcades and amusement attractions where another named leisure format is not more informative. Children's play centres and permanent theme parks have their own categories; general entertainment does not establish an attraction operator.

Provision of arts and craft experiences, workshops or leisure activities. Excludes a business primarily retailing finished goods or craft supplies. Includes participatory craft workshops, creative leisure sessions and similar customer experiences. Sales of art materials or hobby products use retail; production of content for customers or owned publications belongs in media activities.

Operation of children's indoor play, activity and party centres. Excludes childcare, clinical care, tutoring and sports coaching as the main activity. Can combine with Cafes and Coffee Shops for a distinct cafe operation. Includes play-centre and children's activity-venue operators, often with party services. An independently substantial cafe can be combined; childcare, tutoring and clinical support are different activities despite sharing an audience.

Operation of a venue primarily hired for functions, weddings or events. Excludes event catering without a venue. Includes wedding, conference and private-function venues where hiring and operating the space is primary. Add Catering or Event Planning and Coordination only for a distinct service supplied by the business itself.

Operation of gambling services or venues. Excludes newsagencies primarily retailing lottery products; the label does not imply a licence. Includes businesses operating gambling services or dedicated gambling venues. Lottery-product retail can instead be a newsagency/lottery outlet activity; category selection does not confirm permission to conduct a particular activity.

Operation of a gym, fitness centre or sports facility. Excludes businesses primarily selling sporting products. Includes gym operators, fitness centres and businesses running sports facilities. Personal or sports services without a facility may fit Recreation and Sports Services; sale of exercise equipment alone belongs in retail.

Operation of theatres, live music and performance venues. Excludes hospitality-led bars and businesses primarily supplying performers to other venues. Includes theatres, live-music spaces and other performance-venue operators. Supplying performers, running hospitality-led bars, selling recorded media and producing content for clients are different activities; a venue property alone is insufficient.

Operation of pubs, bars, nightclubs and similar venues primarily serving drinks or nightlife entertainment. Accommodation-led hotels use c0007. Includes pub, bar and nightclub operations primarily earning from on-site drinks and nightlife services. Accommodation-led hotels and packaged-liquor shops remain separate, even where the same business name includes the word hotel.

Provision of recreation, sport or fitness activities not better described by a specific leisure category. Excludes clinical treatment and equipment-only retail. Use for recreation, coaching and sports services not captured by a named venue or activity category. Equipment shops, clinical practices and hire-only businesses have different scopes, even when their products or clients are sporting.

Provision of recreational water activities and marine leisure experiences. Excludes boat sales, technical marine services and sea transport. Examples include organised water-sport and marine recreation experiences. Boat dealers, technical marine contractors and passenger transport are different roles; equipment ownership or a waterfront location alone does not identify an experience business.

Provision of accounting, tax preparation and related accounting practice services. Prefer Bookkeeping where routine transaction records are the main service. Includes accounting practices whose core services extend beyond maintaining transaction records, including business accounts and related professional work. Bookkeeping-only operations, lending and investment businesses should use their actual service category.

Provision of bookkeeping, payroll processing and routine financial recordkeeping services. Excludes broader accounting practices as the main activity. Includes outsourced bookkeeping, payroll administration and routine financial recordkeeping. Broader accounting practices and general back-office outsourcing are different scopes; software used to perform the work does not make it a software-product business.

Intermediary services arranging transactions between buyers and sellers, such as business brokerage. Prefer Real Estate and Property Management for real estate agencies. Includes intermediaries primarily arranging business or other non-specialist transactions. Use Finance, Insurance or Real Estate for the named specialist activity; holding or selling the operator's own assets is not brokerage alone.

Provision of outsourced administration, customer support and back-office operations. Prefer a named professional practice where that is the main service. Includes outsourced administrative processes, customer support and operational back-office services. Professional advice, recruitment and named accounting/bookkeeping services remain separate; a business client base alone does not establish professional advisory work.

Civil engineering design, assessment and consultancy services. Excludes businesses primarily delivering construction works. Includes civil engineering advice, design and assessment supplied to clients. Delivering the resulting construction works is a different activity.

Provision or arrangement of finance and related financial services. Excludes accounting-only, insurance-only and general transaction brokerage businesses. Includes lending and finance-arrangement businesses and related specialist services. General bookkeeping, insurance, transaction brokerage and owned software tools have separate scopes; identify the financial service actually supplied to customers.

Professional or business advisory services not better described by a named profession. Excludes known specialist activities and general manual services. Use for professional or advisory services without a more informative named discipline. Routine outsourced operational work uses Business Process Outsourcing; a professional client base alone does not turn manual services into advisory work.

Insurance brokerage, agency and related insurance service businesses. The category does not imply regulatory authorisation. Includes insurance agencies, brokers and related insurance-service operations. The classification concerns the business activity and does not imply an insurer relationship, authorisation or a particular distribution arrangement.

Provision of legal practice and related legal advisory services. Excludes general business consultancy. Includes legal practice businesses and specialist legal advisory services for clients. General business consulting and document printing are different activities; ownership of a legal-sector technology product alone is not a legal practice.

Marketing, advertising, campaign and promotional services across digital and other channels. Excludes operating owned publications or supplying media production alone. Includes agencies providing marketing strategy, advertising, search, social and other campaign services. Channel terms remain aliases; operating owned content or supplying stand-alone media production is a separate activity rather than an automatic agency classification.

Photography, video, audio and editorial content production for customers. Owned publications and content businesses use Publishing and Content Businesses; advertising-led campaign services use Marketing and Advertising Services. Includes commissioned photography, video, audio and editorial production for clients. Owned publications use Publishing and Content Businesses; the category follows the service supplied rather than incidental rights retained in the produced work.

Physical security, guarding, monitoring and related security services. Excludes cybersecurity and businesses primarily installing alarm equipment. Includes guarding, monitoring and physical-security service operations. Installation of alarm equipment and cybersecurity have their own categories; selling a security product without providing the service is a separate role.

Customer printing, copying, document finishing and signage production or installation. Excludes paper manufacture and photographic services as the main activity. Includes printing, copying, finishing and signage supplied to customers. Separate customer production from installation-only work and paper manufacture; product materials alone do not identify the commercial role.

Operation of owned publications, media channels, content libraries or audience businesses, including digital and subscription content. Customer media production uses Media Production Services; excludes software products and advertising agencies. Includes owned publications, channels, newsletters and content libraries monetised through audience, access or publication revenue. Production supplied to clients uses Media Production Services; retaining creative rights alone does not establish an owned publishing operation.

Recruitment, employment placement, labour hire and related staffing services. Excludes training-only and general education businesses. Includes recruitment agencies, placement businesses and staffing or labour-hire operations. Training candidates is a separate activity when primary; an employer's own internal hiring does not establish a recruitment business.

Scientific testing, laboratory, research or technical consultancy services. Excludes medical patient care and general software services. Includes laboratory testing, scientific research services and technical scientific consulting for clients. Patient diagnostics and environmental-specialist advice have named categories; equipment sales alone does not establish a scientific service.

Retail sale of art, craft materials, hobby supplies and related specialist goods. Excludes primarily providing workshops or experiences and ordinary electronics or sporting-goods retail. Includes shops selling art materials, crafts and hobby products. Paid creative workshops or experiences can be another activity when independently substantial; the customer experience should not be inferred merely from the goods sold.

Retail of the operator's own goods primarily through an online shop. May combine with a product retail category. Excludes marketplaces connecting independent sellers and software products. Includes online shops primarily selling their own stock to consumers, with or without operating premises. Product categories can add useful detail; distinguish this trading role from marketplaces, software products and owned publications.

Retail sale of consumer electronics, entertainment products and technology equipment. Excludes IT consulting, software services and entertainment venues. Includes shops selling electronics and entertainment products, including recorded media and associated equipment. Selling products is distinct from publishing content, producing media for clients and operating entertainment venues.

Retail sale of clothing, footwear, fashion accessories, bags and luggage. Excludes manufacture. Combine with a repair category only for a distinct repair service. Includes consumer clothing, footwear, accessories, bags and luggage shops. A luggage-repair workshop is a service activity; wholesale-only supply and making garments are not retail simply because the products are fashionable.

Retail preparation and sale of cut flowers and floral arrangements, with related plants or gifts. Plant propagation uses Plant Nurseries; mixed garden-product retail uses Garden Centres. Includes flower shops primarily preparing and retailing arrangements, with related plants or gifts. Plant production and broad garden-product retail remain distinct; a shared range of plants does not make all three business formats equivalent.

Consumer retail of furniture, furnishings and household goods. Excludes hardware/building supplies and manufacture as the main activity. Can combine with Ecommerce Retail when operating an online shop. Includes consumer furniture, furnishings and household-goods stores. Hardware/building-material retail, making products, styling services and equipment hire are different roles; select additional categories only for genuinely separate operations.

Retail sale of a mixed range of plants, garden goods and supplies through a garden centre. Plant propagation and production use Plant Nurseries; cut flowers and arrangements use Florists. Includes retailers offering plants alongside a mixed range of garden goods. Establish whether the business primarily resells products, grows plants or supplies a service; production-led nurseries and cut-flower florists remain separate.

General retail of goods where no more specific product category applies. Excludes wholesale, manufacturing and service-only businesses. Use for mixed or other consumer retail without a suitable named product category. Identify the main product range before choosing this residual; it should not be used to bypass a known furniture, food or other specialist retail category.

Retail sale of hardware, tools and building materials. Excludes manufacturing, construction contracting and wholesale-only supply. Includes retail hardware, tool and building-material suppliers. Wholesale-only trading, making components and installation contracting are different activities; the product family and trading role should both be clear.

Consumer retail of health, beauty and personal-care products. Excludes pharmacies, treatment services and trade-focused beauty product supply. Includes consumer shops selling beauty, personal-care and health-related goods outside pharmacy scope. Trade supply to salons belongs in Beauty Product Wholesale; treatments, patient services and manufacture remain separate activities.

Operation of a newsagency or lottery product retail outlet. The category does not imply a lottery appointment or other authorisation. Includes newsagency and lottery-product retail operations, including outlets primarily earning from lottery retail. Search vocabulary may include familiar lottery brands; neither the category nor an alias establishes a provider appointment.

Retail sale of office stationery, consumables and office supplies. Excludes general copying and printing services. Includes retail businesses primarily supplying stationery, office consumables and associated everyday supplies. Trade-only distribution and customer printing services are different roles; use a separate category only for a genuinely distinct additional activity.

Retail sale of pets, animal products and pet supplies. Excludes boarding, grooming and other animal care services. Includes shops primarily selling pets, animal products and associated supplies. Clinical veterinary care, grooming and overnight boarding have separate categories; stock sold incidentally to a service does not necessarily justify another activity.

Operation of a pharmacy retail and dispensing business. The category does not imply any registration, ownership eligibility or dispensing authority. Includes businesses operating pharmacy retail and dispensing services. Medical practices, general health-product shops and wholesale supply remain separate; classification does not determine any professional or ownership requirements.

Propagation and growing of plants for sale, including wholesale and sales through an associated nursery. Mixed retail of plants and garden goods without plant production uses Garden Centres; flower arranging and floral retail use Florists. Includes propagators and growers selling their plants wholesale or through an associated nursery. A mixed garden retailer without plant production is a Garden Centre; a florist primarily supplies cut flowers and arrangements.

Operation of a postal service outlet or postal agency business. The category does not imply a postal agency appointment. Includes businesses operating postal counters or agency outlets as their core activity. A substantial separate retail range can be another activity; holding postal-related property or providing general courier transport alone is different.

Retail sale of sporting goods, fitness equipment, camping and outdoor recreation products. Excludes gyms, coaching and operating leisure experiences. Includes sporting, fitness, camping and outdoor-product shops. Coaching, gym operations and recreational experiences are services rather than retail; classify an online shop with Ecommerce Retail only where the online sales activity is real.

Operation of vending machines selling goods to consumers. Excludes manufacture or servicing of vending equipment as the main activity. Includes operators earning from goods sold through vending machines. Manufacturing machines, maintaining equipment or licensing a brand alone are different operations; automated delivery does not identify the specific goods being sold.

Supply and sale of agricultural machinery and equipment. Excludes machinery manufacture and repair-only service businesses. Includes dealers and suppliers of tractors, farm machinery and agricultural equipment. Manufacturing equipment or operating a maintenance workshop is a different activity; incidental servicing does not necessarily require an additional classification.

Contract agricultural work and rural support, including harvesting, mustering, shearing, wool services and breeding support. Excludes farming production, equipment supply, irrigation and forestry as the main activity. Includes crop, livestock and farm-support contracting such as harvesting, mustering, shearing and breeding support. Rural wildlife work belongs here when supplied as farm support, rather than as a recreational hunting or visitor experience.

Supply of agricultural consumables such as fertilisers, seed and farm inputs. Excludes agricultural equipment dealers and farm contracting. Includes suppliers of farm inputs such as seed, fertiliser and agricultural consumables. Determine whether the operation sells goods, manufactures them or applies them as a contract service; a Fertiliser label alone does not identify that role.

Farming of aquatic organisms, including fish, shellfish and aquatic plants. Excludes wild-catch fishing and marine leisure activities. Includes cultivation of fish, shellfish and other aquatic organisms as primary production. Wild-catch fishing, seafood retail and visitor experiences are different activities; identify whether the business grows, catches, trades or hosts customers.

Wild-catch fishing and associated commercial harvesting. Excludes aquaculture, seafood retail and recreational fishing tours. Includes commercial harvesting of wild fish and other aquatic resources. Distinguish catching from aquaculture production, processing and consumer retail; a related product or supply chain does not make those the same activity.

Primary agricultural production through crop or mixed farming where no more specific farming category applies. Excludes rural contracting alone. Includes crop producers and mixed farms without a more specific production category. Contract harvesters and input suppliers provide services or goods to farms rather than necessarily operating the underlying farm production business.

Dairy farming and primary milk production. Excludes processing or retail sale of dairy products as the main activity. Includes farm businesses whose main output is milk from dairy animals. Processing milk into packaged products, distributing dairy stock and selling to consumers are different stages rather than automatic dairy-farming classifications.

Commercial forestry, timber harvesting and forestry contracting. Excludes timber product manufacturing and general garden maintenance. Includes forestry management, commercial timber harvesting and associated contracting. Growing other farm crops, making timber products and selling finished furniture are different activities even when the supply chain is related.

Raising, breeding or dealing in livestock. Prefer Dairy Farming when primary milk production is the main activity. Includes livestock breeding, raising and trading operations. Identify whether the business produces animals, deals in stock or supplies a supporting service; specialist dairy production and contract rural services have their own categories.

Repair, refurbishment and resale preparation of electronic devices. Excludes ordinary new-device retail and materials recovery without device reuse. Includes repair and refurbishment of electronic devices for customers or onward resale. New-device retail, machinery service and recovery of materials without preserving reusable devices are different activities.

Hire of equipment and goods without primarily providing an operator. Prefer Car Rental for passenger vehicles; excludes accommodation and property leasing. Includes businesses hiring equipment or goods without primarily supplying an operator. Car rental, self-storage and accommodation are different formats; equipment used by a contractor to deliver a service is not itself a hire business.

Entertainment services supplied to events or clients, such as performers and event entertainment. Excludes operating a fixed leisure venue as the main activity. Examples include performers and entertainment suppliers engaged for events. Planning the event, operating a venue, catering and hiring equipment without performers are different activities, even when sold to the same wedding or corporate customer.

Planning, styling and coordination of weddings, private functions and business events. Excludes operating a venue, supplying performers, catering or equipment hire alone; combine categories for distinct additional activities. Includes wedding and event planning, coordination and styling services supplied to clients. Venue operation, performer supply, catering and equipment hire are separate activities.

Repair of goods and equipment not better described by a specialist vehicle, machinery or other repair category. Use for repairs to goods without a suitable named vehicle, machinery or electronics category. Examples may include specialist bag or household-item repair; retail product sales and manufacturing are separate roles.

Provision of laundry, garment care and dry cleaning services. Excludes general building cleaning and vehicle washing. Includes laundromats, commercial laundry, dry cleaning and garment-care operations. General building cleaning and machine sales are separate activities; the goods or premises being cleaned help distinguish the actual service.

Maintenance, repair and servicing of machinery and equipment. Excludes equipment manufacture and agricultural machinery dealers. Includes workshops and technical contractors maintaining industrial or agricultural machinery. Manufacturing equipment and dealing in new or used machinery are separate roles; choose a named specialist repair category where more informative.

Passenger or freight transport by air. Excludes aircraft maintenance, agricultural aerial contracting and recreational flight experiences. Includes businesses primarily carrying passengers or freight by air. Agricultural aerial contracting, aircraft maintenance, dealership operations and visitor tours must be distinguished by what is actually sold to customers.

Passenger transport by bus or coach, including charter services. Excludes tour operators primarily selling an integrated tour experience. Includes operators carrying passengers through bus, coach and charter transport. A business mainly selling a guided tour experience can use Tours and Experiences; vehicle hire without a driver is a different role.

Collection and delivery of parcels, documents and small consignments through a courier service. Excludes freight forwarding without delivery operations. Includes delivery networks and contractors moving parcels, documents and small consignments. Freight forwarding, warehousing and general heavy freight remain separate; add them only where the business operates those distinct services.

Freight forwarding and logistics coordination. Prefer a transport mode category for a business primarily carrying the freight itself. Includes arranging freight movements, documentation and logistics between carriers and customers. Distinguish coordination from operating trucks or a warehouse; inventory handling and order fulfilment can be separate substantial activities.

Operation or management of vehicle parking facilities. Excludes vehicle storage offered only as part of an unrelated business. Includes paid parking and contracted operation of parking facilities. Storage of personal goods and self-storage units are different services; incidental customer parking at another business is not a separate parking operation.

Passenger or freight transport by rail. Excludes rail engineering and construction services. Includes businesses primarily carrying passengers or goods by rail. Engineering, construction, rolling-stock supply and maintenance are different activities, even when all customers operate in the rail sector.

Carriage and distribution of goods by road, including truck operations. Excludes courier-only, freight forwarding-only and warehousing-only businesses. Includes road carriers earning from moving goods, including truck and related freight operations. Identify what is carried and whether the operator supplies carriage, coordination or storage; passenger transport and vehicle trading remain distinct.

Passenger transport by taxi, limousine, chauffeur or booked car service. Excludes self-drive rental and bus or coach transport. Includes taxi, chauffeured, limousine and booked-car passenger operations. Vehicle sales, bus/coach transport and self-drive rentals remain separate; classify the service delivered to passengers rather than the vehicle used.

Storage, inventory handling, order fulfilment and third-party logistics services for trade customers. Excludes consumer self-storage and freight-only transport. Includes trade warehousing, inventory handling, pick/pack and third-party fulfilment. Storage and order processing differ from freight coordination or carriage; customer-controlled self-storage units are another service format.

Passenger or freight transport by sea or waterways. Excludes boat sales, technical marine services and recreational experiences. Includes commercial waterborne passenger and freight carriage. Recreational experiences, boat sales and marine technical work have different scopes; distinguish transport sold to customers from a vessel used within another operation.

Provision of hosted computing, cloud infrastructure and website hosting services. Excludes owning a SaaS application without primarily selling hosting. Includes infrastructure, website hosting and cloud-capacity services supplied to customers. A hosted application sold to end users is SaaS rather than infrastructure hosting; the two can be separate activities where both are substantial.

Provision of cybersecurity products or services protecting information systems and data. Excludes physical security and ordinary IT support without a security focus. Includes businesses primarily supplying information-security products, assessments, monitoring or support. Generic customer IT support and physical guarding remain separate; a security feature in an unrelated product does not establish a cybersecurity business.

Provision of data engineering, analytics or AI services for customers. Excludes calling an ordinary business AI-enabled and owned subscription products better described as SaaS. Includes customer data engineering, analytics and artificial-intelligence project or service operations. Distinguish supplying these services from using them internally, and from operating an owned software product or content business.

Ad hoc and ongoing management, implementation and support of customer IT systems. Prefer a named specialist category for cybersecurity, hosting, telecommunications or development as the main activity. Excludes owned software products. Includes customer IT help, implementation, maintenance and ongoing managed support. Owned software products, hosting, development and security-specialist operations have named categories; recurring contracts alone do not define a separate category.

Operation of a digital platform connecting independent buyers and sellers. Excludes an online shop selling the operator's own stock and ordinary software subscriptions. Includes operating a platform that intermediates transactions between independent buyers and sellers. A shop selling its own stock is Ecommerce Retail; ordinary hosted software without that intermediary role belongs in the relevant product category.

Operation of owned software or application products, including desktop and mobile products, outside the more specific SaaS and Online Marketplaces categories. Excludes development for customers. Delivery platform alone does not create another category. Includes owned licensed, desktop and mobile software products outside SaaS and marketplace scopes. Establish product ownership and delivery model; customer development, content publishing and ordinary use of software by another business are different activities.

Operation of owned hosted software products sold by subscription. Other owned applications use Software and App Products; marketplaces and customer development use their own categories. Can combine with Health Technology for a distinct healthcare product focus. Includes the operator's own hosted subscription software, rather than customer projects or subscription content alone. Establish product ownership, access model and the service supplied; operating online alone does not identify a software business.

Design, development or maintenance of software for customers. Prefer Web Design and Development for primarily web-focused work; owned software uses Software and App Products or SaaS. Includes customer-funded software design, development and maintenance projects. Ownership of reusable tools does not by itself establish a product business; a separately operated software product can be another activity when substantial.

Provision, installation, maintenance or consulting for telecommunications networks and communication systems. Excludes owned media publishing and ordinary IT support. Includes network/service operations and communications installation, maintenance or consulting. Establish whether the business operates connectivity, advises clients or works on customer systems; ordinary software support and content publishing remain separate.

Design, development or maintenance of websites and web applications for customers. Excludes owned software or content businesses and hosting-only services. Includes agencies and contractors building or maintaining customer websites and web applications. Hosting, marketing and owned content can be separate activities; the use of a website by any business does not make it a development provider.

Care and support primarily serving older people, where residential nursing care, home/community support or another named activity is not more informative. Use Residential Aged Care or Home and Community Care when that service is primary. Examples include older-person day support and care coordination where no named delivery category is more precise. An older client base alone does not turn property management, equipment retail or clinical treatment into this activity.

Multidisciplinary allied health practices and allied health services not better described by a named specialist practice. Prefer Physiotherapy, Occupational Therapy or another named practice when primary. Excludes general medical practices and non-clinical support. Use for allied-health practices spanning several disciplines or a discipline without a named category. A predominantly named practice should select that specialty; broad clinical and non-clinical support categories are not interchangeable.

Provision of audiology, hearing assessment and associated hearing services. Excludes general electronics retail. Includes hearing assessment and audiology-service businesses with associated patient support. General electronics sales and manufacture of devices are different operations.

Provision of dental clinical services. Excludes dental equipment supply and general healthcare businesses. Includes general and specialist dental practice businesses and associated patient services. Equipment distributors and product laboratories are not patient-care practices; a category label does not identify professional permissions or treatment outcomes.

Support services primarily for people with disability. Prefer a named clinical practice for clinical services; no funding or registration status is implied. Includes non-clinical assistance, personal support and participation services primarily for people with disability. Serving these clients does not by itself establish a medical practice, aged-care operation or a particular funding arrangement.

Clinical healthcare not better described by a named practice or facility category, including other medical specialist and outpatient services. General primary-care practices use General Medical Practices; named allied health practices, hospitals and non-clinical support use their own categories. Use this residual human clinical category only when no named practice or facility is suitable, for example another specialist outpatient service. Identify the actual service; animal healthcare, general primary care and non-clinical support have separate scopes.

General medical primary-care practices providing consultations and treatment by medical practitioners. Other specialist clinical services use General Clinical Healthcare unless a more specific category applies. Excludes hospitals and allied health-only practices. Examples include general primary-care and family medical clinics. Distinguish primary care from specialist outpatient services, diagnostic facilities and multidisciplinary allied-health practices by the main service actually supplied to patients.

Supply of technology products or technical services specifically for healthcare. Can combine with a software or equipment activity when useful. Excludes businesses primarily treating or supporting patients. Includes healthcare-specific software, technical systems and equipment-service products. Identify whether the business owns products, develops for clients, supplies devices or provides patient care before choosing an additional category.

Personal care and support delivered in a person's home or community. Prefer Disability Support Services where disability support is primary; excludes residential nursing homes. Includes personal care, daily-living assistance and community support outside residential nursing facilities. Identify the client group and actual service; home delivery and older customers do not turn support into residential or clinical care.

Operation of a hospital or facility primarily providing hospital-level patient services. Excludes outpatient-only medical practices. Includes operating hospital services and their integrated patient facilities. The category is for the care operation, rather than a building, medical equipment supplier or management consultancy serving hospitals.

Provision of patient diagnostic testing, pathology or medical imaging services. Excludes general scientific laboratories and sale of diagnostic equipment. Includes businesses primarily supplying patient diagnostic testing or imaging services. General scientific laboratories and diagnostic-product suppliers have different roles; treating all medical-sector businesses as the same activity loses this distinction.

Provision of occupational therapy practice services. Excludes employment recruitment and general disability support without occupational therapy services. Includes occupational-therapy practice businesses and related patient services. Staffing placement, disability support and equipment sales remain distinct; serving similar clients does not make those operations occupational therapy.

Provision of optometry and optical dispensing services. May combine with a product retail category where a separate retail activity is significant. Includes optometry practices and optical dispensing operations. Establish whether clinical services, consumer product sales or both are substantial.

Provision of physiotherapy practice services. Excludes massage-only businesses and equipment suppliers. Includes physiotherapy practice businesses and their patient-service operations. A multidisciplinary clinic can identify another substantial practice activity; general fitness, massage and equipment sales should not be assumed from the clinical label.

Provision of podiatry practice services. Excludes footwear retail and general personal care. Includes podiatry practice businesses and related patient-service operations. Footwear retail and general personal care remain separate; a mixed practice should add another category only for a distinct substantial service.

Provision of psychology, counselling or related mental health practice services. Excludes general wellbeing products and non-clinical support as the main activity. Includes psychology, counselling and related mental-health practice businesses. General personal support, wellbeing products and clinical software suppliers have different scopes; identify the service actually provided rather than the audience alone.

Operation of residential aged care primarily providing ongoing nursing and personal care. Excludes independent retirement living. The main operation combines residential accommodation with ongoing nursing and personal care. Retirement living, home support and ownership of a care property alone are different activities, even where the customers are older people.

Operation or management of a retirement living community. Excludes a business primarily delivering residential nursing care. Focuses on operating and managing retirement living, rather than clinical treatment or nursing care. Accommodation ownership alone is not enough, and the category does not identify a particular ownership or resident-contract model.

Provision of speech pathology practice services. Excludes general tutoring and non-clinical support. Includes speech-pathology practice businesses and related patient services. Education, tutoring and non-clinical disability support can serve similar customers while remaining different business activities.

Installation, servicing and maintenance of alarm and electronic physical-security systems. Excludes guarding and cybersecurity services. Includes installing, supporting and maintaining electronic alarm or physical-security systems. Physical guarding, cybersecurity and fire-protection services have different scopes; identify the system and service rather than assigning every safety business to alarms.

Delivery of building and construction works. Excludes businesses primarily providing design or consultancy rather than construction. Includes contractors primarily delivering building projects and construction works. A named trade should be preferred when primary; property investment, design advice and routine household maintenance are different activities.

General building repairs and maintenance not primarily a specialist trade. Excludes garden-only maintenance and integrated facilities management. Includes businesses mainly supplying general building repairs and multi-task maintenance. Garden-only work, a named specialist trade and coordinated facilities management have more informative scopes; identify the work rather than the property alone.

Delivery of civil construction and infrastructure works. Use Civil Engineering Consultancy for engineering design and advisory work. Examples include contractors delivering roads, infrastructure and other civil works. Physical delivery of works is distinct from engineering design and consultancy; equipment sales and routine household maintenance are also different roles.

Electrical installation, contracting, testing and maintenance services. Excludes electrical equipment manufacture and vehicle auto electrical work. Includes electrical contractors primarily supplying installation, maintenance and related technical services at customer sites. Equipment manufacture, specialist renewable/charging/storage operations and unrelated trade work must be distinguished by the actual activity.

Installation, inspection and maintenance of fire protection and safety systems. Excludes general guarding, medical care and emergency public services. Includes fire-system installation, inspection and maintenance businesses. Identify whether alarms, suppression systems or broader fire-safety servicing are primary; physical guarding and general security equipment installation are different activities.

Provision of gardening, landscaping or grounds maintenance services. Excludes plant retail and agricultural crop services. Examples include lawn maintenance, gardening and landscaping contracts. Plant production, garden-product retail and irrigation-specialist work are separate scopes; an agricultural contracting business should use its rural activity instead.

Installation, maintenance and repair of heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration systems. Excludes equipment manufacture. Includes HVAC and refrigeration installation, maintenance and repair businesses. Distinguish the technical service from general electrical contracting, equipment retail and manufacture, even where the same products or customer sites are involved.

Installation and maintenance of domestic, landscape or agricultural irrigation systems. Excludes industrial water treatment. Additional categories can identify a distinct agricultural or landscaping activity. Includes irrigation contractors serving gardens, landscapes, farms or several customer sectors. Selling equipment alone, operating a water utility and supplying unrelated landscaping or farm services are different activities.

Painting, decorating and associated surface-finishing services for buildings. Excludes vehicle refinishing. Includes building painting, decorating and related surface-finishing contractors. Product retail, industrial manufacture and vehicle refinishing have different scopes; choose the actual service rather than the paint or coating material alone.

Plumbing, drainage and related installation or maintenance services. Excludes industrial water treatment and irrigation as the main activity. Includes plumbing and drainage contractors supplying installations, repairs and maintenance. Identify the actual trade service; customer-site work does not make the operator a general builder, water utility or irrigation specialist.

Installation, repair and maintenance of roofing, gutters, cladding and associated building exteriors. Excludes general construction as the main activity. Includes contractors specialising in roofs, gutters, cladding and related exterior work. Separate contracting from selling materials or manufacturing components; a generic construction category does not automatically cover every repair-only service.

Provision of welding and related metal joining or fabrication services. Prefer a named manufacturing category where complete product manufacture is the main activity. Includes welding contractors and fabrication-service workshops primarily supplying skilled joining or metalwork services. Manufacture of complete machinery or metal products can be a separate activity; identify what is delivered rather than the material alone.

Supply, installation, operation or maintenance of energy storage systems. Excludes general battery retail without an energy-storage service focus. Includes businesses supplying, installing, operating or maintaining battery energy-storage systems. Establish the commercial role and system focus; ordinary battery-product retail, general electrical contracting and generation-only operations are different activities.

Operation, installation or maintenance of EV charging infrastructure as the main business. Excludes general vehicle sales and electrical contractors without a charging focus. Includes businesses operating charging networks or primarily installing and maintaining charging infrastructure. Distinguish operating a charging network from installation and maintenance; supplying equipment alone does not establish this service activity.

Operation of energy generation or supply businesses. Excludes primarily installing customer energy systems and upstream oil/gas extraction. Includes operating energy-generation or energy-supply businesses. Establish whether the operator generates, supplies, installs or maintains systems; fuel extraction and customer installation contracting are separate stages.

Environmental assessment, monitoring and advisory services. Excludes waste collection and materials recovery operations. Includes specialist environmental assessments, monitoring and advisory services supplied to clients. Physical waste collection, remediation operations and resource recovery are different activities.

Oil and gas extraction, processing or specialist support operations. Excludes retail vehicle fuel stations. Includes upstream oil/gas operations and specialist processing or support businesses. Fuel retail and general electricity supply have separate scopes; renewable generation cannot be assigned here simply because both activities concern energy.

Recovery of reusable materials from waste or end-of-use products. Excludes ordinary waste collection without recovery and businesses primarily manufacturing new goods. Includes businesses recovering reusable materials and preparing resources for further use. Producing new finished goods and collecting waste without recovery are different activities; a generic manufacturing or freight category is not an automatic substitute.

Installation, maintenance and support of renewable energy systems, including solar and wind. Excludes electricity generation/supply and businesses primarily providing EV charging or battery storage services. Includes specialist solar, wind and comparable renewable-system service businesses. Distinguish installation/maintenance from generating or selling energy, and identify any separate charging or storage operation rather than assuming every energy business is electrical contracting.

Collection, handling and management of waste. Prefer Recycling and Resource Recovery where materials recovery is the main activity. Includes businesses whose main role is waste collection, handling or management. Recovery of reusable material is separate when primary; operating collection vehicles does not automatically make the business a general freight carrier.

Industrial water supply, treatment or processing operations. Excludes domestic pool maintenance and garden irrigation. Includes operating industrial water-supply, treatment and related processing services. Selling water-treatment equipment alone, maintaining pools and installing farm or garden irrigation systems are different commercial roles.

Animal care, grooming and related services. Prefer Pet Boarding for overnight pet boarding; excludes animal retail and veterinary clinical services. Includes non-clinical pet-care services such as grooming, washing, day care and training. Overnight boarding and veterinary clinical work have named categories.

Temporary boarding and overnight care of pets. Excludes breeding, animal retail and veterinary practices. Includes boarding kennels and catteries whose main service is temporary overnight accommodation. Day grooming and clinical veterinary care remain separate; a combined operator can identify those activities independently.

Provision of veterinary clinical services for animals. Excludes pet retail, boarding and non-clinical grooming or care. Includes clinical animal-health practice businesses. Non-clinical grooming, boarding and product retail remain separate; a substantial independently operated retail or boarding service can be an additional activity when justified.

Commercial, domestic and specialist cleaning of buildings and facilities. Excludes laundry/dry cleaning, vehicle washing and specialist pest control. Includes businesses mainly cleaning buildings, premises and facilities for clients. Garment care, vehicle washing and specialist pest management have named scopes; equipment sales alone does not establish a cleaning-service business.

Coordinated management of building operations and contracted maintenance services. Excludes a single specialist trade and real estate sales agencies. Includes businesses coordinating building operations and several maintenance/service contracts. Pure real estate agency, strata administration and a single trade have separate scopes; a management activity is not established by property ownership alone.

Pest management, inspection and treatment services. Excludes agricultural hunting/trapping and general cleaning as the main activity. Includes pest inspection, prevention and treatment businesses for buildings and other customer sites. General cleaning, garden maintenance and agricultural wildlife contracting have different scopes; the relevant service must be identified.

Pool, spa and associated domestic water-system cleaning and maintenance services. Excludes industrial water treatment and irrigation contracting. Includes pool and spa cleaning, routine maintenance and associated domestic system services. Construction of a pool, industrial water treatment and irrigation contracting are different activities rather than automatic extensions of maintenance.

Real estate agency, property management and related property service businesses. Excludes a property asset sale without an operating service business. Includes real estate agencies and third-party property management services. Facilities coordination, strata administration and accommodation management rights have separate scopes; a sale of property without an operating service business is not enough.

Operation of customer-controlled storage units and associated storage services. Excludes trade warehousing and vehicle parking as the main activity. Includes operating customer-accessed storage units and associated self-storage services. This differs from hiring equipment, managing property for others and handling trade inventory; the operated storage service matters rather than property ownership alone.

Administration and management services for strata or community-title schemes. Excludes accommodation management rights and property asset sales. Includes administrative and management services for strata and community-title schemes. Accommodation letting, general tenancy management, coordinated maintenance and property investment are different roles, even when conducted for the same building.

Operates under a franchise agreement using an established brand and business system. Combine with the activity actually carried out, such as food service, retail or cleaning. This characteristic does not identify the industry, distinguish a new franchise opportunity from an existing business, or establish the terms or transferability of the agreement.

Operates principally from a residential home rather than dedicated commercial premises. Combine with the goods or services the business provides. Home administration alone does not establish that an otherwise premises-based operation is home based. This characteristic does not imply that the home is included in the sale or that the business is relocatable.

Conducts a substantial part of its core business through websites, apps or other online channels. It can apply to retail, software, content or services when online delivery or transactions are central to the operation. A marketing website alone is insufficient. Dedicated premises can also apply; this characteristic does not identify an activity or imply an online-only business.

Delivers its core goods or services by travelling to customers or operating from a vehicle or movable unit. Combine with the actual activity, such as repairs, food service or cleaning. Routine delivery by a premises-based business does not by itself establish a mobile operation. Mobility does not imply that the business can transfer to another service territory.

Can transfer its operating base to another location while retaining the core business being offered. Use where the seller has established that the relevant customer relationships, assets and operating arrangements can support a move. Home-based, online or mobile operation alone is insufficient. This characteristic does not promise that a transfer is unrestricted or cost free.

Offers the operating business together with ownership of the property used by that business as part of the sale. Combine with the operating activity. Leasing or occupying premises alone does not qualify, and a separate optional property opportunity should be described according to the actual sale arrangement. This characteristic does not cover a property-only sale.

Has an owner actively involved in day-to-day operation or delivery of its core goods or services. Combine with the business activity. This characteristic describes the current operating arrangement, rather than a promise about a buyer's future workload. An owner can work alongside a manager; owner involvement and under-management arrangements are not automatically mutually exclusive.

Has a manager responsible for day-to-day operations while the owner primarily provides oversight. Combine with the business activity and verify the actual division of responsibilities. An owner may still work in the business. This characteristic does not promise passive income, an absent owner, guaranteed staffing continuity or a particular future workload for the buyer.

Uses dedicated operating premises, whether leased or owned, for a substantial part of its core activity. Combine with the goods or services provided. A business may also operate online or deliver mobile services. Occupying premises does not mean ownership of the property is included in the sale; use Business with Property only for that separate fact.
